dial.summary: BTC Accumulation holds on Sep 12 as hot CPI (+3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM, Sep 11) drove FOMC hike probability to 85% and pushed real yields to ~2.59% (headwind), with the 2Y surging +22bps to 4.61% and compressing 2s10s to +36bps (now neutral); BTC.D surged to 59.2% in a defensive crypto rotation while TOTAL edged up to $2.8T and stablecoin dominance continued its 30-day slide to 10.9%, keeping BTC accumulation dynamics intact ahead of the FOMC/BOE/BOJ decision cluster Sep 16–18.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) estimated at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; 6–8 week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); MacroMicro confirmed June 2026 global G4 M2 at $102,663.81B ($102.66T); 4-week uptrend confirmed (June $102.66T → July ~$103.4T = +$0.74T, above flat threshold); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); September monetary policy context: ECB hiked Sep 10, FOMC Sep 16 with hike probability surging to 85% following hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM, Sep 11) and Aug PPI (+5.4% YoY, Sep 10), BOE Sep 17, BOJ Sep 18; a synchronized hike cycle would apply modest G4 M2 headwinds via higher reserve costs through Q4 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp (no new ISM release since Sep 1); status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY, +0.4% MoM, Sep 11) adds cost-push pressure to manufacturing sector, though Production at 58.3% indicates robust factory output; next ISM Manufacturing release October 1 (September data); S&P Global Flash PMI Sep 23 will provide the next advance manufacturing-sector read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.09 on September 12, 2026 — essentially unchanged from 99.06 (Sep 11) despite 2Y yields surging +22bps to 4.611% after hot Aug CPI (+3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM); DXY's muted response to a hawkish CPI print reflects dollar-negative cross-currents (yen carry unwind risks ahead of BOJ Sep 18, policy divergence uncertainty); 4-week trend down: ~99.60 (Aug 12 per barchart technical analysis) → 99.09 (Sep 12) = −0.51%, just above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY 99.09 within 97.5–100 band); FOMC hike probability at 85% (CME FedWatch, Sep 12) — a Sep 16 hike + hawkish dot plot would test the 100 headwind threshold; August 2026 DXY averaged 100.12, ranging 98.73–101.73 (barchart); BOJ Sep 18 outcome is the primary downside DXY risk via potential yen carry unwind.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: Estimated real yield: ~2.59% for Sep 12 (derived: 10Y nominal 4.97% − BEI 2.38% = 2.59%; cross-checked against direct DFII10 of 2.46% on Sep 9, 2026 per WatchGold — the +13bp move Sep 9→12 reflects the bond selloff accelerating post-CPI); Aug CPI released Sep 11: +3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM — monthly print more than quadrupled July's +0.1%; FOMC hike probability jumped to 85% (from 57% Sep 11); 4-week trend up: ~2.43% (Aug 12 est.) → ~2.59% (Sep 12) = +16bps, well above 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); 10Y nominal 4.97% approaching psychologically significant 5% level; FOMC Sep 16 dot plot is the primary catalyst — a hike + hawkish 2027 projections would push real yields further above 2.5%.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 12, 2026: 2s10s spread at +0.36% (+36bps) — sharp bear flattening from yesterday's +43bps (Sep 11); Sep 12 data: 10Y yield ~4.97% (+1bp), 2Y yield 4.611% (CNBC, 12:45 PM EDT, +22bps on the day after hot Aug CPI +3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM drove FOMC hike probability to 85%); spread = 4.97% − 4.611% = +35.9bps, reported as +0.36%; 4-week trend flat: ~+35bps (Aug 12 estimate) → +36bps (Sep 12) = +1bp in 4 weeks — below the steepening threshold; status neutral (positive spread but 4-week steepening condition not met; shifted from supportive on Sep 11; status rule: supportive requires positive AND steepening); today's bear flattening is driven by 2Y pricing in 85% hike probability, not by falling long-end rate-cut expectations; FOMC Sep 16 is the key risk: a hike would further flatten the curve as 2Y prices above current levels.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6.74T (~$6,737B) for week ending September 3, 2026 (H.4.1 confirmed); H.4.1 for week ending September 10 is scheduled for release September 17, 2026 — not yet available (will reflect post-ECB Sep 10 hike and pre-FOMC Sep 16 reserve conditions); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 6 estimate) → $6.74T (Sep 3) = +$40B, within flat threshold; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; routine measured QT continues with no acceleration and no overnight rate spike); FOMC Sep 16 decision will inform any policy shift on balance sheet normalization pace; next confirmed update September 17 (H.4.1 release for week ending Sep 10).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate approximately +0.01% per 8h (Sep 12, 2026; CoinGlass and MacroMicro direct fetch egress-blocked; value based on prior confirmed data and market context — BTC holding near $77,000 on Sep 12 post-CPI); 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August–September 2026; BTC.D surged to 59.2% (from 57.2% Sep 11) as altcoins sold off faster than BTC following hot CPI; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding confirms spot-driven price action, not leveraged long crowding; BTC.D rise reflects quality rotation, not leveraged BTC positioning); TOTAL rose to $2.8T (+2.78% on the day) while BTC held near $77K — market absorbed hot CPI without a major derisking funding spike.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$306B (Sep 12, 2026; CoinGecko); total crypto market cap $2.8T (Sep 12: +2.78% on the day — market absorbed hot Aug CPI +3.4% YoY and 85% FOMC hike probability with resilience); stablecoin dominance 10.9% ($306B / $2.8T) — down from 11.2% (Sep 11) as TOTAL rose while stablecoin supply held flat; 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% early August 2026 to 10.9% = sustained ~3pp decline confirming continued capital deployment into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply: today's dominance decline on rising TOTAL confirms healthy risk-on capital flows within crypto; BTC.D at 59.2% and TOTAL at $2.8T are mutually consistent with defensive within-crypto rotation).

upcoming.title: Empire State Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Empire State Manufacturing Business Conditions Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — one of the earliest September manufacturing reads, released the day before FOMC Day 2; August 2026 survey showed prices paid surging to 58.6 (from 52.3 in July), inventories at -5.2, and new orders softening; a strong September reading would reinforce the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop heading into FOMC Sep 16; a sharp decline would introduce doubts about the manufacturing recovery sustainability; leading indicator for ISM Manufacturing (next release October 1).

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve FOMC rate decision at 2:00 PM ET (two-day meeting Sep 15–16), press conference at 2:30 PM ET; includes updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) with dot plot; current target range 3.5%–3.75%; market-implied hike probability surged to 85% (CME FedWatch, Sep 12) following Aug CPI +3.4% YoY / +0.4% MoM (Sep 11), Aug PPI +5.4% YoY (Sep 10), and Aug NFP +162K beat (Sep 4); dot plot and 2027 rate path guidance are the primary DXY, real yield, and risk-asset drivers for Q4 2026; a hike + hawkish dots would push 10Y above 5% and real yields further above 2.5%; a surprise hold with dovish commentary would be the most risk-on outcome for crypto.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Retail Sales for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — released same day as FOMC decision (2:00 PM ET); prior July advance retail sales were +0.1% MoM; strong Aug NFP (+162K) suggests continued consumer income growth supporting spending; a strong retail sales print (+0.3% MoM or above) confirms Q3 consumer resilience and may reinforce the Fed's inflation-fighting case; a weak print (below 0%) would suggest consumer fatigue despite labor market strength, potentially complicating the Fed's policy calculus ahead of the 2:00 PM decision.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization for August 2026 at 9:15 AM ET — released same day as FOMC; measures output of manufacturing, mining, and electric and gas utilities; a strong reading would reinforce ISM Manufacturing's expansion signal (54.6 in August) and reduce near-term recession concerns; capacity utilization approaching 80% would add to inflationary pressures and potentially reinforce the FOMC hike case; context: Aug PPI energy component surged (diesel +24.1% MoM) due to Middle East conflict spillovers — watch energy sector output.

upcoming.title: Bank of England Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee rate decision at 12:00 PM London time (7:00 AM ET) — one day after FOMC Sep 16; BOE currently holds at 3.75% (July 30 MPC vote 6-3 to hold); UK CPI elevated at 2.9% YoY in July driven by Middle East energy spillover; with ECB having hiked Sep 10 and FOMC hike probability at 85%, a BOE hold with dovish guidance would create significant transatlantic monetary policy divergence driving GBP/EUR and GBP/USD volatility; a surprise BOE hike would confirm the global tightening cycle remains synchronized; BOE outcome will significantly influence risk sentiment in the back half of September.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Housing Starts and Building Permits for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for residential construction activity and broader economic momentum; released same day as BOE decision; higher rates (FOMC hiking Sep 16 at 85% probability) weigh on housing affordability; a decline in starts or permits would add to evidence that elevated financing costs are cooling the housing sector despite a resilient labor market; 30Y fixed mortgage rates have been elevated in the 6.5–7.5% range throughout 2026.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Survey (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — a leading indicator for national ISM Manufacturing (next release Oct 1); released alongside Housing Starts and Initial Jobless Claims; a strong Philly Fed print would reinforce the ISM-above-50 expansion backdrop and reduce near-term recession risk; released the day after FOMC, so any reaction to the Sep 16 rate decision may feed into September manufacturing sentiment; context: Aug CPI showed gasoline prices drove 1/3 of the monthly MoM increase (+3.9%), which may show up in manufacturing costs.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 13, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 13, 2026 — first labor market read post-FOMC Sep 16; any significant spike above 220K would amplify rate-path repricing following the FOMC decision; prior week (Sep 6) approximately 206K; released alongside BOE rate decision, Housing Starts, and Philly Fed — a busy data morning one day after the FOMC.

upcoming.title: Bank of Japan Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting September 17–18, with Statement on Monetary Policy expected September 18 — two days after FOMC Sep 16; BOJ has been normalizing policy in 2026 (hiked June 16); any surprise hike or hawkish commentary would strengthen JPY and potentially trigger yen-carry-trade unwinds with broad impact on global risk assets including crypto; DXY at 99.09 on Sep 12 (neutral band 97.5–100) — a hawkish BOJ would accelerate dollar weakness toward the supportive sub-97.5 threshold; the full ECB (Sep 10 hike confirmed) + FOMC (Sep 16, 85% hike probability) + BOJ (Sep 18) sequence is the most synchronized global monetary policy event cluster of the cycle and will set the tone for Q4 2026.
